newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden Centre Party head to announce his future.
newsitem.headline: Sweden Centre Party head to announce his future.

text.p: The leader of Sweden's Centre Party, Olof Johansson, said on Thursday he would hold a press conference at 1330 GMT to announce his decision about whether he will stay on as leader of the party.

Johansson promised to make a decision about his future after Easter after heavy criticism about falling voter support for the Centre Party that has cooperated informally with the minority Social Democratic government.
At the last general election in September 1994 the Centre Party secured 7.7 percent of the vote, the third largest party in the seven party parliament.
But a poll in late March showed the party's support was now below six percent, falling 1.7 percentage points since January this year.
The Centre Party has cooperated informally with the ruling centre-left Social Democrats in the seven party Swedish parliament.

Earlier this year the Social Democrats, Centre and Left parties joined forces on a new energy agreement that will see the closure of one of Sweden's 12 nuclear reactors next year and a second closure in 2001.
Johansson has been leader of the Centre Party for 10 years and at 59 is the oldest of all Sweden's political party leaders.
